meteorShowers.title: Orionid Meteor Shower Peak
meteorShowers.japanese: オリオン座流星群 · 極大
meteorShowers.visibilityNote: ZHR ~ 25 meteors/hr at 66 km/s. Debris stream from Halley's Comet leaving persistent ionized trails.
meteorShowers.description: Fast, bright meteors radiating from northern Orion near Betelgeuse. Best observed after midnight when the radiant climbs high into the southeastern sky.

meteorShowers.title: Northern Taurid Fireball Swarm
meteorShowers.japanese: おうし座北流星群 · 火球
meteorShowers.visibilityNote: Rich in slow, brilliant yellow-orange bolide fireballs slicing near the Pleiades cluster.
meteorShowers.description: While modest in hourly numbers, the Northern Taurids are renowned for producing pebble-sized fragments that flare into dazzling multi-second fireballs.

meteorShowers.title: Leonid Meteor Shower Vigil
meteorShowers.japanese: しし座流星群 · 疾風
meteorShowers.visibilityNote: Hyper-velocity meteors (71 km/s) with blue-green magnesium vapor trains under favorable quarter-moon skies.
meteorShowers.description: Among the fastest meteor streams known to astronomy, encountering Earth head-on from the Sickle of Leo in the pre-dawn hours.

meteorShowers.title: Geminid Sovereign Meteor Shower
meteorShowers.japanese: ふたご座流星群 · 大極大
meteorShowers.visibilityNote: Premier shower of 2026 with ZHR up to 150/hr. Waxing crescent moon sets early, leaving pristine dark skies.
meteorShowers.description: Dense rocky debris shed by asteroid 3200 Phaethon produces multicolored white, yellow, and emerald meteors throughout the entire winter night.

meteorShowers.title: Ursid Winter Solstice Shower
meteorShowers.japanese: こぐま座流星群 · 冬至
meteorShowers.visibilityNote: Circumpolar northern radiant visible all night across the Northern Hemisphere.
meteorShowers.description: Strictly northern-sky shower peaking on the winter solstice, radiating beside the Little Dipper's bowl.

meteorShowers.title: Quadrantid New Year Meteor Surge
meteorShowers.japanese: しぶんぎ座流星群 · 初星
meteorShowers.visibilityNote: Sharp 6-hour peak with ZHR ~ 120/hr and frequent bright blue fireballs.
meteorShowers.description: Named after the obsolete constellation Quadrans Muralis, the Quadrantids rival the Geminids during their brief, intense pre-dawn climax.

meteorShowers.title: Lyrid Spring Celestial Shower
meteorShowers.japanese: こと座流星群 · 春宵
meteorShowers.visibilityNote: ZHR ~ 18/hr with occasional surges up to 100/hr. Radiant sits beside brilliant Vega.
meteorShowers.description: Chronicled by East Asian court astronomers since 687 BCE, Lyrid meteors streak out from the harp of Orihime-boshi.

meteorShowers.title: Eta Aquariid Halley Stream
meteorShowers.visibilityNote: Exceptionally dark New Moon skies in May 2027 allow up to 50 earth-grazer meteors/hr.
meteorShowers.description: Spring counterpart to the Orionids, famous for long, dramatic earth-grazing meteors skimming the eastern horizon before dawn.

meteorShowers.title: Perseid Summer Festival Shower
meteorShowers.japanese: ペルセウス座流星群 · 夏夜
meteorShowers.visibilityNote: ZHR ~ 100/hr. First-quarter moon sets around midnight, leaving dark post-midnight skies.
meteorShowers.description: Warm summer night spectacle producing prolific, colorful meteors and lingering ionization trails along the northern Milky Way.

eclipses.title: Total Lunar Eclipse (Blood Moon)
eclipses.japanese: 皆既月食 · 赤銅の満月
eclipses.visibilityNote: Fully visible across Japan, East Asia, Australia, the Pacific, and western North America.
eclipses.description: The Full Worm Moon plunges deep into Earth's umbral shadow for 58 minutes of totality, glowing copper-crimson in the evening sky.

eclipses.title: Total Solar Eclipse
eclipses.visibilityNote: Path of totality crosses Greenland, Iceland, the Atlantic Ocean, and northern Spain.
eclipses.description: The Moon completely obscures the solar photosphere for 2 minutes 18 seconds, revealing the pearly solar corona near sunset over Europe.

eclipses.title: Deep Partial Lunar Eclipse (93% Umbral)
eclipses.japanese: 部分月食 · ほぼ皆既
eclipses.visibilityNote: 93% umbral immersion visible across the Americas, Europe, Africa, and the central Pacific.
eclipses.description: Nearly a total lunar eclipse: 93% of the Moon's diameter enters Earth's dark inner shadow, casting a dramatic red-charcoal gradient across the lunar disc.

eclipses.title: Annular Solar Eclipse (Ring of Fire)
eclipses.japanese: 金環日食 · 黄金の環
eclipses.visibilityNote: Annularity path spans Chile, Argentina, the South Atlantic, and West Africa (7m 51s duration).
eclipses.description: At apogee, the Moon silhouettes inside the solar disk, creating a blazing golden ring of fire for nearly eight minutes.

eclipses.title: Full Snow Moon Penumbral Eclipse
eclipses.japanese: 半影月食 · 銀影の月
eclipses.visibilityNote: 92% penumbral magnitude; dusky shading along the Moon's southern limb across Europe, Africa, Asia, and Americas.
eclipses.description: The Moon glides deeply through Earth's outer penumbral shadow, dimming the southern lunar highlands with a silver-tea patina.

eclipses.title: Great Total Solar Eclipse of the Century
eclipses.japanese: 世紀の皆既日食 · 大コロナ
eclipses.visibilityNote: 6 minutes 23 seconds of totality across southern Spain, North Africa, Egypt (Luxor), and Arabia.
eclipses.description: One of the longest total solar eclipses of the 21st century, plunging ancient temples along the Nile into over six minutes of coronal twilight.

eclipses.title: Penumbral Lunar Eclipse
eclipses.visibilityNote: Visible across East Asia, Australia, the Pacific Basin, and North/South America.
eclipses.description: Subtle penumbral grazing of the Full Sturgeon Moon across the Pacific celestial hemisphere.
